In 1923, a jockey won a horse race, while he was already dead.
Frank Hayes was a twenty two year old stable hand. He had never won a single race.
Then he got his big chance, riding a horse called Sweet Kiss, at Belmont Park in New York.
Nobody believed in them. The odds were twenty to one.
To make the weight limit, Frank went on a brutal crash diet, and lost a lot of weight in just a few days.
The race began. Twelve jumps, and Sweet Kiss was flying.
But somewhere in the middle of the race, Frank had a heart attack.
His body slumped forward, but he did not fall. He stayed in the saddle.
And Sweet Kiss kept running, jump after jump, with a dead man on her back.
She crossed the finish line first.
When the owner ran over to congratulate him, he found out that Frank was dead.
Frank Hayes was buried in his racing silks. And the horse got a new name. Sweet Kiss of Death.
